title: Triple Integrals in Cylindrical and Spherical Coordinates
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Cylindrical Coordinates Volume Element
definitions.latex: dV = r \, dz \, dr \, d\theta, \quad x = r\cos\theta, \; y = r\sin\theta, \; z = z
definitions.statement: Cylindrical coordinates combine polar coordinates in the xy-plane with standard Cartesian height z. The volume element dV = r dz dr dtheta includes the polar Jacobian factor r.
definitions.explanation: Ideal for solid regions exhibiting symmetry about the z-axis, such as cylinders, cones, and paraboloids.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Converts radial cross-sections into simple rectangular integration limits.

definitions.title: Spherical Coordinates Volume Element
definitions.latex: dV = \rho^2 \sin\phi \, d\rho \, d\phi \, d\theta, \quad x = \rho\sin\phi\cos\theta, \; y = \rho\sin\phi\sin\theta, \; z = \rho\cos\phi
definitions.statement: In spherical coordinates, rho is distance from the origin, phi is polar angle from the positive z-axis, and theta is azimuthal angle in the xy-plane. The volume element is dV = rho^2 sin(phi) drho dphi dtheta.
definitions.explanation: The factor rho^2 sin(phi) derives from the Jacobian determinant of the spherical coordinate transformation.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Essential for central potentials, spheres, and conical volumes.
